name: Rothay Riverside Loop
description: The club's default easy evening: out along the River Rothay, around the Under Loughrigg lane and back over the stone footbridge. Barely a climb worth naming, though the two short rises past Fox How will still say hello. Runnable end to end in road shoes unless the river has been up.

name: Loughrigg Terrace Circuit
startPoint: White Moss car park, between Rydal and Grasmere
description: A proper little circuit with one honest pull up to Loughrigg's summit cairn, then the famous terrace path with Grasmere laid out below. Steep and loose in places on the drop to Rydal Cave, and worth every step of it. Trail shoes recommended after rain.

name: Wansfell Round
description: Up the stone steps out of town and onto Wansfell Pike the direct way — half an hour of proper climbing, no apologies — then over the top and down through Troutbeck's lanes and Skelghyll Woods. The summit view down the length of Windermere is the photo every club member has.

name: Fairfield Horseshoe
description: The classic horseshoe over eight named tops: up by Nab Scar and Heron Pike, along the ridge to Fairfield's broad summit plateau, then back over Hart Crag, Dove Crag and the Pikes. This is serious mountain running — navigation gets genuinely hard on Fairfield's plateau in mist. Full fell kit, no exceptions.

name: Langdale and Elterwater Long Round
description: Our long steady one: valley tracks and bridleways linking Elterwater, Great Langdale, Little Langdale and Skelwith. Nothing steep and nowhere technical — just honest distance with the Langdale Pikes for company the whole way round. Two sensible exit points if the day stops being fun.
